verdict_rationale: All 5 Round-1 performance findings are RESOLVED in tree (SLOs filled to 32/33 µservices; canonical 4-window burn-rate present; Sweep-I tier helpers adopted by 10+ values.yaml; oya-shared-hyperscaler-metrics-{kernel,adapter-prometheus} present and building; cross-microservice-latency-budget.md authored at docs/standards/). However, ADR-0145 reform shipped without propagating into capacity-models (zero µservice capacity-model.md cites ADR-0145), no spec/registry artifact codifies the 3 invariants for CI enforcement, the operator-facing changelog for ADR-0145 is missing, and Fix-E is NOT done — three Rust skeleton crates (oya-resolve-scorecards-app, oya-gen-microservice-manifests-app, oya-check-adr-placeholders) have only Cargo.toml and no src/. All 4 Python scripts remain in scripts/ and remain executable. Recommendation: approve PR #143 with a follow-up IP for (a) capacity-model ADR-0145 propagation, (b) ADR-0145 operator changelog, (c) Rust-primary Python retirement (Fix-E completion).

The 9 previously-empty dirs (PR R1 sample) all have at least 6 openslo.yaml files; foundry has 14 (largest surface, expected).

new_capacity_findings_post_reform.title: ADR-0145 reform has not propagated to any µservice capacity-model.md
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.evidence: grep -rl 'ADR-0145' microservices/*/capacity-model.md → 0 matches. cell, governance, audit-chain, ontology, workflow-studio capacity-models contain ZERO references to the new direct-µservice-to-µservice mTLS/Cedar/audit-emit pattern. The 'workflow as opt-in mediator' shift fundamentally changes audit-chain fan-in (every µservice now emits its own seal vs. centralized at Workflow), Cedar authz call rate (every inter-µservice call gets per-call evaluation now), Ontology write traffic (every µservice projects vs. mediated through Workflow), and cell SPIFFE-ID issuance burst (every µservice handshake → cell, not just Workflow→sibling).
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.recommendation: Author follow-up IP to update 5 capacity-models with ADR-0145-reform sections: (a) cell — SPIFFE-ID issuance rate now O(N²) edges between µservices, not O(N) through Workflow; (b) governance — Cedar authz QPS is now ≈ Σ inter-µservice call rate; (c) audit-chain — fan-in is now Σ-of-µservices, not Workflow-mediated; (d) ontology — write rate now Σ-of-µservices projecting canonical entities; (e) workflow-engine — SLO is now its own concern (was platform SLO ceiling).

new_capacity_findings_post_reform.title: ADR-0145 invariants 1-3 have no CI enforcement
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.evidence: ADR-0145 §Decision declares 3 enforcement lanes: oya-check-audit-chain-seal-coverage, oya-check-otel-trace-propagation, oya-check-ontology-projection-coverage. None of these crates exist (find crates -name 'oya-check-audit-chain-seal-coverage' → empty). Without enforcement the reform is doctrine without teeth; µservices added in future shards may forget the invariants.
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.recommendation: File follow-up IP scaffolding 3 check crates + wiring to oya-dev-cli gate command + adding 3 lanes to .github/workflows/ci-lane-*.

new_capacity_findings_post_reform.title: Cedar per-call inter-µservice authz latency budget unspecified
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.evidence: ADR-0145 requires Cedar policy authorization on every direct sibling call but docs/standards/cross-microservice-latency-budget.md Flow-A per-hop budgets don't include the Cedar PEP overhead. If Cedar adds 5-10ms per hop at p99, the 1000ms social-fanout budget may be tight. governance/capacity-model.md does not declare Cedar QPS at scale (cross-µservice authz rate ≈ total RPS × N_neighbors).
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.recommendation: Add a 'Cedar PEP overhead' row to each per-hop budget allocation in cross-microservice-latency-budget.md; declare Cedar QPS in governance/capacity-model.md.

new_capacity_findings_post_reform.title: Workflow µservice SLO posture undefined under ADR-0145
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.evidence: Under ADR-0145, Workflow becomes opt-in (AWS Step Functions analog). Its SLO becomes its own concern, not a platform SLO ceiling. But microservices/workflow-engine/slos/*.openslo.yaml were authored under the pre-reform assumption that Workflow was the mediator. The 6 SLO files at microservices/workflow-engine/slos/ should be re-verified that p99 targets reflect the new opt-in load profile (likely lower QPS than pre-reform, but each invocation may be a long-running saga with different tail behavior).
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.recommendation: axis-workflow-engine + ops-sre-reliability re-validate workflow-engine SLO targets under opt-in saga workload, NOT mediator workload.

new_capacity_findings_post_reform.title: Ontology write-path scaling under decentralized projection
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.evidence: ADR-0145 invariant 3 mandates every canonical-entity-owning µservice projects to Ontology. ontology/capacity-model.md line 82 sizes 2500 reads/sec/replica × 800 replicas at L tier = 2M reads/sec — but write-path sizing under the new pattern (where every µservice issues projection writes directly, not through Workflow buffering) needs explicit per-source-µservice rate. Without buffering, write bursts can exceed coordinator capacity.
new_capacity_findings_post_reform.recommendation: ontology/capacity-model.md add a 'projection-write fan-in' section enumerating which µservices project + their declared write rates, validate Citus coordinator headroom under sum-of-rates.

findings.title: No rollback strategy documented for ADR-0145 reform
findings.evidence: ADR-0145-inter-microservice-communication-reform.md contains §Consequences but no §Rollback. The reform retires feedback_workflow_objectgraph_adapter_layer auto-memory and changes networkpolicy egress rules (direct sibling allowed). If reform produces problems on dev, `git revert` works on doctrine but does NOT auto-revert networkpolicy YAML changes already applied to running clusters. The reform also retires Workflow as universal mediator — any µservice that has begun bypassing Workflow needs a migration-back path.
findings.recommendation: Add §Rollback to ADR-0145 documenting: (a) revert PR + apply prior networkpolicy YAML to restore deny-direct-sibling default; (b) interim-state risk window during revert; (c) audit-chain seal pattern compatibility (must accept both calling-µservice-emitted seals AND Workflow-mediated seals).

findings.title: No operator-facing changelog for ADR-0145
findings.evidence: find docs -name '*ADR-0145-operator*' → 0 matches. ADR-0145 is the canonical decision doc but is too dense for an SRE rolling out the change. No companion `docs/operators/ADR-0145-operator-changelog.md` or equivalent describes the day-2 impact (e.g., 'You will see new direct egress traffic between sibling µservices; Cedar authz alerts now fire on per-call basis; audit-chain fan-in increases by ~Nx').
findings.recommendation: Author docs/operators/ADR-0145-operator-changelog.md with: (a) what changed observationally; (b) new alert patterns; (c) dashboard panels to add; (d) escalation paths under reform; (e) rollback procedure.

findings.title: No migration plan for existing µservices to adopt ADR-0145 invariants
findings.evidence: ADR-0145 requires existing µservices to: (a) wire in oya-shared-hyperscaler-metrics-kernel, (b) update networkpolicies for direct sibling egress, (c) author Cedar fragments for sibling-µservice principals, (d) wire in oya-shared-audit-chain-client-kernel (invariant 1), (e) wire in oya-shared-tracing-client-kernel (invariant 2), (f) declare ontology_projections in manifest.json (invariant 3). No per-µservice IP enumerates this 6-step migration. The 33 µservices in tree have not been audited against the invariants.
findings.recommendation: File follow-up IP per-µservice (or one bulk IP) tracking adoption of the 6-step migration. Add lane-blocker once enforcement crates exist (PERF-R2-002).

findings.title: Grafana dashboards exist for canonical alerts but not for ADR-0145 reform-specific signals
findings.evidence: microservices/observability/dashboards/ contains gate-eligibility.json, operator-burn-rate.json, tenant-slo-overview.json (3 dashboards). These cover canonical SLO/burn-rate views but no dashboard surfaces 'direct sibling egress rate per µservice pair' or 'Cedar PEP latency per inter-µservice call' or 'audit-chain fan-in per source µservice' — all of which become operationally critical under ADR-0145.
findings.recommendation: Author 3 additional Grafana dashboards: (a) inter-µservice-egress-traffic.json, (b) cedar-pep-latency.json, (c) audit-chain-fanin-by-source.json.

findings.evidence: ADR-0139 (agentic SLO-gated promotion) is Accepted and defines SloTargetRepository + BurnRateEvaluator + EligibilityLedgerWriter ports. dev branch is canonical; promotion to staging requires SLO burn-rate green per soak window. PR #143 lands on dev (per CLAUDE.md branch model) and will be subject to ADR-0139 admission gate before any cross-environment promotion. This is sufficient canary coverage.

findings.evidence: ls crates/oya-resolve-scorecards-app/src → empty directory does not exist; only Cargo.toml present. Same for oya-gen-microservice-manifests-app and oya-check-adr-placeholders. Cargo.toml declares [lib] path = 'src/lib.rs' and [[bin]] path = 'src/main.rs' — building these crates will FAIL with file-not-found.

Not blockers (pre-existing infrastructure), but listed for completeness against the Rust-primary directive.
findings.recommendation: Schedule into masterplan; not gating for PR #143 merge.

findings.title: oya-dev-cli should be sole entrypoint for programmatic gate/validator/generator concerns
findings.evidence: User-asked question. Recommendation: YES — oya-dev-cli is the sole programmatic Rust entrypoint for gates/validators/generators. Standalone app crates (oya-resolve-scorecards-app, oya-gen-microservice-manifests-app) should fold into oya-dev-cli as subcommands (e.g., `oya-dev-cli resolve-scorecards`, `oya-dev-cli gen-microservice-manifests`) for consistency with `oya-dev-cli gate` and `oya-dev-cli vcs`. Standalone bin entries fragment the surface and dilute the 'one Rust CLI' user experience. Standalone library crates (oya-shared-*, oya-check-*) are fine — they are units of code reuse; the CLI binary should be singular.
findings.recommendation: Fold the 3 in-progress app crates into oya-dev-cli subcommands when porting from Python.
